title: Markup Matryoshka
one_liner: Peel back the stacked margins inside one AI token, from the foundry to the chipmaker to the AI lab.
speaker: Dave Blundin
context: Dave argues that a token's price stacks a lab margin of about 80–85% on a chipmaker margin of about 80–85% on a foundry margin of about 50%. He predicts vertical integration will squeeze these layers.
demo: Nested dolls or rings show the foundry, chip and lab layers, with a slider for each layer's margin. Visitors drag the sliders or click 'vertically integrate' to merge layers and see the illustrative token price shrink. A side panel shows the share of the final price that comes from manufacturing versus markup.
data_plan: Margin figures as stated on the podcast as defaults. The cost base and the share of token cost from chips are user-adjustable and labeled as simulated assumptions.
risks: Gross margins at different companies sit on different cost bases, and chips are only part of what serving a token costs, so simple stacking overstates the effect. The page needs a clear 'illustrative toy model' label.

acceptance: Dragging the lab margin slider from 85% to 20% visibly shrinks the outer ring and lowers the displayed token price
Clicking 'vertically integrate' merges two layers and shows the before/after price
A visible label says the cost base and stacking are a simplified illustration
Defaults load with the margins quoted on the episode, each with its source label
